Rashi on Gittin 59b:10:1.hebrew: א"ל דאורייתא היא - ותורה אמרה כן מפני דרכי שלום:
Rashi on Gittin 59b:10:1.english: [Rav Yosef] said to him: It is by Torah law - and the Torah said so on account of the ways of peace:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:12:1.hebrew: אלא אמר אביי - דרכי שלום דקתני מתני':
Rashi on Gittin 59b:12:1.english: Rather, Abaye said - [This refers to the] "ways of peace" that the Mishnah teaches:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:12:2.hebrew: לכדמר - אתא, רבה בר נחמני שהיה רבו:
Rashi on Gittin 59b:12:2.english: In accordance with [that of] Mar - [it] comes [to teach; Mar refers to] Rabbah bar Nachmani, who was his [Abaye's] teacher:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:12:3.english: They do not wait - They do not need to wait:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:12:4.hebrew: הבוצע - כגון בעה"ב, שהוא מברך המוציא, ואפי' הוא קטן:
Rashi on Gittin 59b:12:4.english: The one who breaks bread - For example, the homeowner, who recites the Hamotzi [blessing], even if he is younger [or of lesser stature]:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:12:5.english: He extends his hand - into the dish first, to eat with it the slice of Hamotzi [bread]:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:13:1.english: They taught [this] only - that one shows honor to his master:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:13:2.english: Only at a meal - as we said [above]:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:13:3.hebrew: אבל - לענין לקרות בתורה בבית הכנסת, אין כהן חולק כבוד ללוי ולוי לישראל, דלא ליתו שארא לאנצויי ולמימר "אנא נמי קרינא ברישא"; והיינו דקתני מתניתין: "כהן קורא ראשון כו'", כמה שכתוב בתורה, ואינו רשאי לחלוק כבוד בדבר ולשנותו, מפני דרכי שלום:
Rashi on Gittin 59b:13:3.english: But [in the synagogue, one may not] - With regard to reading from the Torah in the synagogue, a Kohen does not yield honor to a Levite, nor a Levite to an Israelite, so that the others will not come to quarrel and say, "I too will read first." And this is what the Mishnah teaches: "A Kohen reads first, etc." — [following the order] as it is written in the Torah, and he is not permitted to yield honor in this matter and alter it, for the sake of the ways of peace:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:16:1.english: We have a tradition - A tradition from our forefathers:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:16:2.hebrew: נתפרדה חבילה - נפסק הקשר, איבד הלוי את כבודו בשביל חבילתו הנפרדת ואינו קורא כלל; כך אמר מורי הזקן ומורי ר' יצחק בן יהודה, וכן סידר רב עמרם, אבל מתלמידי מורי רבי יצחק הלוי שמעתי משמו שאין סדר לדבר להקדים לוי לישראל, ומי שירצה יקדים:
Rashi on Gittin 59b:16:2.english: The bundle is separated - The bond is severed: the Levite has lost his honor on account of his separated bundle, and he does not read at all. So said my elder teacher and my teacher Rabbi Yitzchak ben Yehudah, and so did Rav Amram prescribe [in his order of prayers]. However, from the students of my teacher Rabbi Yitzchak HaLevi I heard in his name that there is no [fixed] order in the matter to give precedence to a Levite over an Israelite, and whoever wishes may take precedence:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:16:3.english: A priest reads - in place of a Levite:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:17:1.hebrew: מפני פגמו של ראשון - שלא יאמרו הראשון אינו כהן; ולקמיה פריך: והא קא חזו דסליק ממנינא:
Rashi on Gittin 59b:17:1.english: Because of the flaw of the first [one] - So that they will not say [that] the first [one] is not a priest; and later [the Gemara] asks: "But don't they see that he counts toward the number [of readers]?"

Rashi on Gittin 59b:17:2.hebrew: משום פגם שניהם - לא ידעי אינשי פגמא בהי מינייהו, ויאמרו: ראשון אינו לוי, לפיכך חזר וקרא לוי; אי נמי: שני אינו לוי אלא ישראל. ולקמיה פריך: גבי כהן נמי, אמאי ליכא נמי פגם שניהם, דאתו למימר שני לאו כהן הוא אלא לוי:
Rashi on Gittin 59b:17:2.english: Because of a flaw in both of them - People do not know which of them has the flaw, and they will say [either that] the first is not a Levite, [and] therefore a Levite was called again to read, or else [that] the second is not a Levite, but rather an Israelite. And later [the Gemara] asks: regarding a priest as well, why is there not also [a concern of] a flaw in both of them, since [people] might come to say [that] the second is not a priest, but rather a Levite:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:17:3.english: With that same priest - [he] himself returns and reads in place of a Levite:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:18:1.hebrew: דמוחזק לן באבוה דהאי שני דכהן הוא - ולא מצי למימר לוי הוא, הלכך לראשון הוא דאיכא פגמא:
Rashi on Gittin 59b:18:1.english: Where we have a presumption concerning the father of this second [one], that he is a priest - And one cannot say [that he] is a Levite; therefore, it is regarding the first [one] that there is a flaw:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:19:1.hebrew: ופרכינן דכוותיה על כרחך גבי לוי דמוחזק לן באבוה דהאי שני דלוי הוא - ומאי פגמא איכא? אלא על כרחך היינו פגמא, דאמרי: אבוה ממזרת נסיב, או נתינה (או) מן הגבעונים שגזר דוד עליהם, ואחליה מקדושת לוייה, והוי ישראל פסול ובמקום ישראל קורא. הכא נמי, גבי כהן שני, אתו למימר כו':
Rashi on Gittin 59b:19:1.english: And we object similarly: Perforce, regarding a Levite, [the case is] that we have a presumption concerning the father of this second [reader] that he is a Levite - And what flaw is there? Rather, perforce, this is the flaw, that [people] will say: His father married a mamzeret, or a netinah (or) from the Gibeonites upon whom David decreed, and [thereby] profaned him from Levite sanctity, so that he is a disqualified Israelite and reads [the Torah] in the place of an Israelite. Here too, [regarding] a second priest, they will come to say, etc.:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:19:2.hebrew: ואחליה - מקדושת כהונה, והרי הוא כישראל:
Rashi on Gittin 59b:19:2.english: And he profaned him - from the sanctity of the priesthood, and behold, he is like an Israelite:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:1:1.hebrew: בור הקרוב לאמה - אמת המים המביאה מים מן הנהר לשדות, ורגילין לעשות בורות, שאם תיבש האמה ימלאו מן הבור וישקו השדות, ומרגילין מי האמה לבור עד שיתמלא. ותקנו חכמים שיתמלאו בורות שבשדות העליונות, שהן קרובין למוצא האמה, ואח"כ ימלאו התחתונים. וכשהוא ממלאו, סוכר את האמה עד שיתמלא:
Rashi on Gittin 59b:1:1.english: A pit near the irrigation channel - [This refers to] a water channel that brings water from the river to the fields, and [people] are accustomed to make pits so that if the channel dries up, they can draw from the pit and water the fields, and they direct the water of the channel into the pit until it fills up. The Sages enacted that the pits in the upper fields, which are near the source of the channel, should be filled [first], and afterward the lower ones should be filled. And when one fills [his pit], he dams the channel until it fills up:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:1:2.hebrew: מפני דרכי שלום - שלא תהא מחלוקת ביניהם לומר "אני אסכור ראשון", דהא תקנתא דרבנן הכי, ואע"פ שאינו דין:
Rashi on Gittin 59b:1:2.english: On account of the ways of peace - So that there should not be a dispute among them, [each saying,] "I will dam [the channel] first," for this is the enactment of the Rabbis, even though it is not [strictly] the law:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:20:1.hebrew: ומשני: הואיל ובלוי קרא, ליכא פגמא, דאי <abbr title="סלקא דעתך">ס"ד</abbr> חלל הוא — סוף סוף לוי מי הוי שיקרא במקום לוי? הלכך על כרחך, כיון דאבוה כהן, אין זה חלל, ואין כאן פגם אלא לראשון:
Rashi on Gittin 59b:20:1.english: And [the Gemara] answers: Since he read [in the Torah] in [the place of] a Levite, there is no [implication of a] flaw [in him]; for if it should enter your mind [that] he is a chalal [a disqualified priest], ultimately, is he a Levite, that he should read in place of a Levite? Therefore, perforce, since his father is a priest, this one is not a chalal, and there is no flaw here except for the first [priest].

Rashi on Gittin 59b:21:1.english: And for whom - Who [would] blemish him:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:21:2.hebrew: אילימא היושבין - עד שיגלל ס"ת:
Rashi on Gittin 59b:21:2.english: If you say [the concern is for] those sitting - [meaning, those who sit] until the Torah scroll is rolled up:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:21:3.english: Behold, they see him - [namely,] this first priest, that he goes up [to be counted] in the count of seven:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:21:4.english: For those who leave - [those] who will not wait and will leave:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:22:1.english: After them - [i.e., after] the priest and the Levite:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:2:1.hebrew: מצודות חיה כו' - מדאוריית', כל כמה דלא מטא לידיה לאו גזל הוא, ובגמ' מפרש ליה במצודות שאין להן תוך דליקני ליה כליו:
Rashi on Gittin 59b:2:1.english: Traps for beasts, etc. - By Torah law, as long as [the trapped creature] has not reached his hand, it is not [considered] robbery; and in the Gemara it explains it [as referring] to traps that do not have an interior such that his vessel would acquire [it] for him:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:2:2.hebrew: גזל גמור - בגמרא מפרש: גזל גמור מדבריהם. וטעמא דרבי יוסי בכולהו, דקסבר עשו — מפני דרכי שלום — את שאינו זוכה לקנות קנין גמור, כזוכה:
Rashi on Gittin 59b:2:2.english: Full-fledged robbery - In the Gemara it explains [that this means] full-fledged robbery by rabbinic decree. And Rabbi Yosei's reason in all of them is that he holds [that the Sages] treated — on account of the ways of peace — one who does not [ordinarily] acquire a full acquisition like one who acquires:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:4:1.hebrew: המנקף - חותך, כמו "ונקף סבכי היער" (ישעיהו י׳:ל״ד), וכמו "ונשאר בו עוללות כנוקף זית" (שם יז):
Rashi on Gittin 59b:4:1.english: Who gleans - [This means] cuts, as in, "And he shall cut down the thickets of the forest" (Isaiah 10:34), and as in, "Yet gleanings shall be left in it, like the beating of an olive tree" (ibid., 17):

Rashi on Gittin 59b:6:1.english: And delivered it - That the priests should read from it [first], and afterward the sons of Levi:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:9:1.english: And you shall sanctify him - [The verse continues:] "For [the bread of your God he offers,] etc.":

Rashi on Gittin 59b:9:2.hebrew: לפתוח ראשון - בכל דבר כבוד, בין בתורה בין בישיבה, הוא ידבר בראש:
Rashi on Gittin 59b:9:2.english: To open first - In every matter of honor, whether in Torah [study] or in an assembly, he shall speak first:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:9:3.english: And to recite the blessing first - at a meal:

Rashi on Gittin 59b:9:4.hebrew: וליטול מנה יפה ראשון - אם בא הכהן לחלוק עם ישראל בכל דבר, לאחר שיחלקו בשוה, אומר לו הישראל: "ברור וטול איזה שתרצה":
Rashi on Gittin 59b:9:4.english: And to take a fine portion first - If [a Kohen] comes to divide [something] with an Israelite in any matter, after they have divided [it] equally, [the Israelite] says to him: "Choose and take whichever [portion] you want."

Tosafot on Gittin 59b:14:1.hebrew: אבל בשני ובחמישי לא - אומר ר"ח: הני מילי לדידהו, דבחול הוו טרידי במלאכתן ולא שכיחי, אבל לדידן שכיחי בשני ובחמישי כמו ביו"ט:
Tosafot on Gittin 59b:14:1.english: But on Monday and Thursday, not - Rabbeinu Ḥananel says: This applies to them, for on weekdays they were occupied with their work and were not commonly present [in the synagogue]; but for us, [people] are commonly present on Monday and Thursday just as on a Festival:

Tosafot on Gittin 59b:15:1.hebrew: דאפי' רבי אמי ורבי אסי כהני חשיבי כו' - משמע דאי לאו הכי אסור, אפי' הוא גדול מכל בני עירו. והא דאמר בסוף מגילה (דף כח.): א"ר פרידא, מימי לא ברכתי לפני כהן, ופריך הש"ס מחכם הקורא אחר כהן עם הארץ דחייב מיתה, ומוקי לה בשוין — ועל כרחך לאו שוין ממש, דא"כ מאי רבותיה? אלא אתא לאפוקי כהן ע"ה, וצריך למימר נמי דכולהו הוו כפופין לרבי פרידא, דאי לאו הכי מאי רבותיה? אי נמי: הא דבעי הכא כייפי, היינו בשבתות ויו"ט, ור' פרידא אפילו בשני ובחמישי לא קרא:
Tosafot on Gittin 59b:15:1.english: As even Rabbi Ami and Rabbi Asi, the most important priests, etc. - This implies that if not for that [fact], it is forbidden even if he is greater than all the people of his city. And [as for] that which it says at the end of Megillah (28a): "Rabbi Preida said: In all my days I never recited a blessing before a priest," and the Talmud challenges [this] from [the teaching about] a sage who reads after an ignorant priest, that he is liable to death, and [the Talmud] establishes it [as referring to a case] where they are equal — perforce [it does] not [mean] literally equal, for if so, what is his distinction? Rather, it comes to exclude an ignorant priest, and one must also say that all of them were subject to Rabbi Preida, for if not for that, what is his distinction? Alternatively: that which [the Gemara] requires here [that they] be subject [to him] is on Shabbatot and Festivals, whereas Rabbi Preida did not read [first] even on Monday and Thursday:

Tosafot on Gittin 59b:16:1.hebrew: נתפרדה החבילה - ה"ר יצחק ברבי יהודה מפרש דקורא לוי במקום הראוי לו. והא דאמר בכתובות (דף כה:): "מוחזקני בזה שהוא כהן, שקרא אחריו לוי" — צריך לומר דקים ליה דלא קרא במקום הראוי, דגדול היה משלפניו או קטן משל אחריו:
Tosafot on Gittin 59b:16:1.english: The bundle is separated - Rabbi Yitzchak bar Rabbi Yehuda explains that a Levite reads in the place fitting for him. And as for that which [the Gemara] says in Ketubot (25b): "I have a presumption regarding this [man] that he is a priest, because a Levite read after him" — one must say that [the witness] knew with certainty that [the Levite] did not read in the place fitting for him, because he was greater than the one before him or lesser than the one after him:

Tosafot on Gittin 59b:17:1.hebrew: כי קאמרינן באותו כהן - למאי דתקון בהקורא את המגילה (דף כא:), שכל אחד מברך לפניה ולאחריה, ניחא. ואפילו לפי מאי דתנן (שם) "הפותח מברך לפניה וחותם מברך לאחריה", צריך לומר באותו כהן שקורא פעמים, שהולך ויושב בינתים; דאי בע"א, במאי הוי מינכרא שתי קריאות? כי ההיא דתניא בתוספתא דמגילה: אם לא היה שם אלא אחד דידע לקרות, קורא ויושב, ועומד וקורא. וזה היה נמי קודם התקנה, דלאחר התקנה, שכל אחד מברך לפניה ולאחריה, לא צריך. ומשם רבינו יהודה כתבו, דאם אין בבית הכנסת רק כהנים, אחד קורא במקום שבעה, ועל כל פרשה יברך לפניה ולאחריה:
Tosafot on Gittin 59b:17:1.english: When we said [we were speaking] of the same priest - According to what [the Sages] instituted in [the chapter entitled] HaKoreh et HaMegillah (21b), that each one recites a blessing before [the reading] and after it, [this] is straightforward. And even according to what we learned in the Mishnah (ibid.), "[He who] opens recites a blessing before it, and [he who] concludes recites a blessing after it," one must say regarding the same priest who reads twice that he goes and sits down in between; for if [it were] otherwise, how would the two readings be distinguishable? [This is] like that which was taught in the Tosefta of Megillah: If there was only one [person] there who knew how to read, he reads and sits down, and stands up and reads. And this too was before the enactment, for after the enactment, when each one recites a blessing before it and after it, this is not necessary. And in the name of Rabbeinu Yehudah they wrote that if there are only priests in the synagogue, one [priest] reads in place of [all] seven, and over each portion he should recite a blessing before it and after it:

Tosafot on Gittin 59b:9:1.hebrew: וליטול מנה יפה ראשון - כגון במעשר עני, או בצדקה אם הוא עני, או בחברים המסובין בסעודה; אבל במידי דשותפות לא, דאמרינן בפ' מקום שנהגו (פסחים דף נ:) דהנותן עינו בחלק יפה אינו רואה סימן ברכה לעולם:
Tosafot on Gittin 59b:9:1.english: And to take a fine portion first - For example, with the poor man's tithe, or with charity if he is poor, or among companions reclining at a meal; but not in a matter of partnership, for we say in the chapter [entitled] Makom Shenahagu (Pesachim 50b) that one who sets his eye on a fine share never sees a sign of blessing:
